blocks.text: The footage Loznitsa uncovered at Rome’s Audiovisual Archive of the Labour and Democratic Movement left him marvelling at the contrast with official Soviet productions from the same era. Opening in Moscow, the film shifts into territories where different traits, beliefs and ethnographic features emerge, revealing the powerful grip of an empire over its people. The result is a compelling indictment of Russia’s historical and present-day imperialism.

blocks.text: Andrey Zvyagintsev transposes Claude Chabrol’s La Femme infidèle to contemporary Russia, delivering a magnificent political allegory that dissects the mechanics of ego, violence and corruption.
My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile

The second part of Julia Loktev’s epic documentary, detailing the persecution of journalists in Russia, follows her brave protagonists’ escape abroad following the country’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Once Upon a Time in Harlem
Filmed by William Greaves in 1972 and completed by his son David 50 years later, this is a rapturous love letter to the Harlem Renaissance.
